abstract_sentences.text: At NeurIPS, Kera et al. (2024) introduced the use of transformers for computing Gröbner bases, a central object in computer algebra with numerous practical applications.

evidence.anchor: introduced the use of transformers for computing Gröbner bases

abstract_sentences.text: In this paper, we improve this approach by applying Hierarchical Attention Transformers (HATs) to solve systems of multivariate polynomial equations via Gröbner bases computation.

evidence.anchor: applying Hierarchical Attention Transformers (HATs)

abstract_sentences.text: The HAT architecture incorporates a tree-structured inductive bias that enables the modeling of hierarchical relationships present in the data and thus achieves significant computational savings compared to conventional flat attention models.

evidence.anchor: achieves significant computational savings

abstract_sentences.text: We generalize to arbitrary depths and include a detailed computational cost analysis.

evidence.anchor: generalize to arbitrary depths

abstract_sentences.text: Combined with curriculum learning, our method solves instances that are much larger than those in Kera et al. (2024).

evidence.anchor: solves instances that are much larger

method_analysis.formal_objects: Field/ring/ideal, Gröbner basis, reduced basis, shape position, token tensor, per-level embedding dimensions, finite-field encoding and axis-wise positional tables.
method_analysis.inputs: Backward-generated system F; padded tree tensor X with axes for equations, terms, and symbols; field q=7 for main experiments.
method_analysis.outputs: Predicted reduced Gröbner basis token sequence; evaluated by exact match, support accuracy and per-token accuracy.
method_analysis.state: Bottom-up intermediate tensors Y^(i), pooled X^(i), and top-down refined tensors Z^(i).
method_analysis.objective: Supervised sequence-to-sequence prediction of the corresponding reduced Gröbner basis; no separate optimization objective is introduced.
assumptions: cost derivation ignores batch size, multi-head attention and pooling

components_and_prior_problem.tree_representation: matches the structured polynomial-system object to mitigate flat sequence explosion
components_and_prior_problem.bottom_up_attention: captures sibling/local relationships and progressively creates parent representations
components_and_prior_problem.top_down_cross_attention: returns parent/global context to lower nodes
components_and_prior_problem.per_level_dimensions: allocates more representational width to upper levels at lower sequence cost
components_and_prior_problem.curriculum: moves training from low-dimensional/sparse systems to higher-dimensional/denser systems
components_and_prior_problem.axis_positional_embedding: encodes multi-axis positions in the tensorized input

method_analysis.action_transition: setup_notation → state_problem → define_component → explain_mechanism → instantiate_algorithm → state_complexity → connect_to_prediction → connect_to_experiment → summarize
method_analysis.algorithm_inventory: No Algorithm environment or pseudocode; formulas (2)–(5) and Figure 1/6 provide the executable data flow.

theory_summary.status: No theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary or proof block appears in the PDF.
theory_summary.core_result: Equations (6)–(8) derive per-level and total HAT computational cost under explicit simplifications; for d_i=d and regular trees, the attention term scales as L^(1+1/n)d rather than L^2d.
theory_summary.assumptions: Batch, multi-head attention and pooling are omitted; the regular-tree comparison is an asymptotic interpretation, not a measured guarantee.
theory_summary.role: core_chain plus explanation; it motivates the architecture but does not prove exact Gröbner correctness, OOD generalization or end-to-end runtime superiority.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Expose the polynomial system’s token→term→polynomial→system tree to a two-phase HAT layer, then use curriculum learning to reach larger and denser systems.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: HAT data flow, cost derivation (1)–(8), Figure 1/2, n=13 Table 1, no-curriculum Table 2 and multi-field Table 3.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Width/depth seeds, n=7/n=10 dynamics, Hi-Transformer, field extension, data configuration, BG/FG statistics, BART, runtime recheck and Table 12 hyperparameters; this preserves method compactness but reduces self-sufficiency for attribution and fairness.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Concrete tree diagram plus matching layer equations, followed by one unified training-dynamics figure and captions defining exact/support/token metrics and timeout rules.
final_judgment.largest_gap: “Beats classical algorithms” and “replacement” rely on GPU inference versus CPU timeout-censored runs, while exact success peaks at 61.2% and the complexity derivation is not independently measured end to end (pp.8, 10).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For structured sequence methods, align object structure, information-flow equations, matched-budget efficiency evidence and component/strategy separation in one causal chain.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule applies when the hierarchy corresponds to a real recursive object; padding, timeout, hardware and offline-training differences must be isolated before treating local-attention complexity as an end-to-end guarantee.
